slides.must: Hook in ≤10 words that names the tension: the dairy swap was easy, the steps changed. Kicker names the dish, the diet and 4 → 6. The photo label must say it is the Original recipe's licensed stock photo, not the adapted dish.
The three real swaps, before → after, shortened faithfully from ingredients[1], [5], [15]. Headline says the list was the easy part.
Broiling: the Original says one baking sheet, 8 to 10 minutes. The rewrite: two batches, same 8 to 10 minutes each. Why: crowding costs the char.
Reducing the sauce: don't multiply the 10 to 15 minutes. A wider pan evaporates faster. Start checking at 10 minutes, go by the spoon trail.
The cream: whisk separated coconut cream smooth, keep the sauce at a gentle simmer, and check several pieces (165°F) rather than stretching the time.
This is a real RecipeFix result: show the app's own result header and its 'What RecipeFix changed' summary. One-line recap a cook can save.

claims.phrasing: Real RecipeFix result (captured 2026-10-21): scaling a dairy-free chicken tikka masala from 4 to 6 servings changed the steps — broil in two batches at the same time per batch, use the spoon trail instead of multiplying the reduction time, let excess coconut yogurt drip off so it chars, keep the coconut cream at a gentle simmer.
It rewrites the cooking steps, not just the ingredient list.
Every change comes with its reason.

copy.caption:
One swap can move the whole method. In this dairy-free chicken tikka masala, scaled from 4 to 6 servings, the ingredient list is simple: coconut yogurt, vegan butter, coconut cream. The steps are where cooks get burned. More chicken needs more broiler space, not a longer blast. A wider pan means you start checking the sauce at 10 minutes and stop when a spoon dragged through leaves a clear trail. Coconut cream wants a gentle simmer. Chicken still needs 165°F in the thickest pieces. This is a real RecipeFix result, so the changed step comes with the reason.
